A JetStream delivery settles on the server: ack acknowledges it, retry sends a negative acknowledgement, drop terminates it. A JetStreamSubject reads a stream through a consumer, and the consumer tracks every message it hands out until the message is settled. The handler's outcome becomes the acknowledgement the server receives. ack sends +ACK, and the consumer moves past the message. retry sends -NAK, and the consumer delivers the message again at once, with its delivery count raised by one. drop sends +TERM, and the server stops delivering the message. In the manual form Ok acknowledges and Err(outcome) settles by the outcome. A delivery nobody settles comes back once the consumer's ack_wait has passed. retry_after asks for the next delivery after a delay, and max_attempts caps how many deliveries one message gets. A Core NATS subscription has no acknowledgement at all: its deliveries are processed at most once.

The first reservation after startup fails while the stock count loads, so its order is delivered again; an order of nothing is terminated. Macros Manual examples/nats_settlement_ack.rs /// Reserves the stock of each order. The outcome settles the delivery on the server: `ack` is /// `+ACK`, `retry` is `-NAK` and the consumer delivers the order again, `drop` is `+TERM`. #[subscriber(JetStreamSubject::new("orders.placed", "ORDERS").durable("fulfilment"))] async fn fulfil(order: &Order, State(warehouse): State<Warehouse>) -> HandlerOutcome { if order.quantity == 0 { tracing::warn!(order.id, "an order of nothing is terminated"); return HandlerOutcome::drop(); } match warehouse.reserve(order).await { Ok(()) => HandlerOutcome::ack(), Err(err) => { tracing::warn!(order.id, %err, "reservation failed, redelivering"); HandlerOutcome::retry() } } } examples/manual/nats_settlement_ack.rs /// Reserves the stock of each order. `Ok` is `+ACK`; `Err(retry)` is `-NAK` and the consumer /// delivers the order again; `Err(drop)` is `+TERM`. struct Fulfil; impl Handle<Order, (), (), (), AppState> for Fulfil { async fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), ctx: &mut Context<'_, (), AppState>, ) -> Result<(), HandlerOutcome> { if order.quantity == 0 { tracing::warn!(order.id, "an order of nothing is terminated"); return Err(HandlerOutcome::drop()); } ctx.state().warehouse.reserve(order).await.map_err(|err| { tracing::warn!(order.id, %err, "reservation failed, redelivering"); HandlerOutcome::retry() }) } }

ack_wait is how long the server waits for a settlement; a delivery left unsettled comes back after it and counts as an attempt. It is a setting of the consumer, so JetStreamSubject carries it, and the server keeps it with the consumer it creates at startup. The default is 30 seconds. The window opens when the server hands out a delivery and closes when the handler's outcome reaches it as an acknowledgement. A delivery still unsettled at the end of the window is delivered again: the handler took longer than the window, or the process stopped before it settled. The handler then sees the same message a second time, with its delivery count raised, while the first run may still be going on. So the window is set longer than the slowest run of the handler. A redelivery after the window counts toward max_attempts, because the count is the server's own. The value is a NonZeroDuration: a literal written with nonzero! is checked while the crate compiles, so a window of zero does not build.

Rendering a long invoice takes up to a minute, so the consumer waits two minutes for the settlement. Macros Manual examples/nats_settlement_ack_wait.rs /// Rendering a long invoice takes up to a minute, so the consumer waits two minutes for the /// settlement before it delivers the request again. #[subscriber( JetStreamSubject::new("billing.requested", "BILLING_REQUESTS") .durable("invoicer") .ack_wait(NonZeroDuration::from_secs(nonzero!(120))) )] async fn render(invoice: &Invoice) -> HandlerOutcome { match render_pdf(invoice).await { Ok(pages) => { tracing::info!(invoice.id, pages, "invoice rendered"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } Err(err) => { tracing::warn!(invoice.id, %err, "invoice not rendered"); HandlerOutcome::drop() } } } examples/manual/nats_settlement_ack_wait.rs /// Rendering a long invoice takes up to a minute, so the consumer waits two minutes for the /// settlement before it delivers the request again. fn invoices() -> JetStreamSubject { JetStreamSubject::new("billing.requested", "BILLING_REQUESTS") .durable("invoicer") .ack_wait(NonZeroDuration::from_secs(nonzero!(120))) } struct Render; impl Handle<Invoice> for Render { async fn handle( &self, invoice: &Invoice, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> Result<(), HandlerOutcome> { match render_pdf(invoice).await { Ok(pages) => { tracing::info!(invoice.id, pages, "invoice rendered"); Ok(()) } Err(err) => { tracing::warn!(invoice.id, %err, "invoice not rendered"); Err(HandlerOutcome::drop()) } } } }

Core NATS stores nothing and acknowledges nothing, so a Core delivery is processed at most once and a retry delivers nothing again. The server hands a Core message to the subscribers connected at that moment and keeps no copy. So settling a delivery of a CoreSubject or a CoreWildcard reports AckError::Unsupported, and the runtime logs it as a warning naming the subscription. The handler's answer still decides what the framework does next. ack and drop end the delivery. A plain retry ends it too: the server has nothing to deliver again, and a message the handler could not process is gone. retry_after, or any retry under a cap, makes the framework publish a copy of the message back to the subject, so the message comes back once. That copy waits in the service's memory, so a process that exits before the delay is over loses it. A message that has to survive a failed handler or a restart is read from a stream through a JetStreamSubject, which settles on the server.

A shipping notice whose mail server does not answer asks for a retry, and the message is not delivered again. Macros Manual examples/nats_settlement_core.rs /// Mails the customer once the order ships. A Core NATS message reaches whoever is subscribed /// at that moment and is not stored, so `retry` here delivers nothing again: the message is /// processed at most once. #[subscriber("orders.shipped")] async fn notify(order: &Shipped) -> HandlerOutcome { match send_mail(&order.email).await { Ok(()) => HandlerOutcome::ack(), Err(err) => { tracing::error!(order.id, %err, "the shipping notice is lost"); HandlerOutcome::retry() } } } examples/manual/nats_settlement_core.rs /// Mails the customer once the order ships. A Core NATS message reaches whoever is subscribed /// at that moment and is not stored, so `Err(retry)` here delivers nothing again: the message is /// processed at most once. struct Notify; impl Handle<Shipped> for Notify { async fn handle( &self, order: &Shipped, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> Result<(), HandlerOutcome> { send_mail(&order.email).await.map_err(|err| { tracing::error!(order.id, %err, "the shipping notice is lost"); HandlerOutcome::retry() }) } }

dead_letter(subject) names the subject a spent delivery is published to; a capped JetStream consumer with none terminates it. It follows max_attempts(n) at the mount site. When a retry would make the delivery the n-th one, the framework settles it and publishes it to the dead-letter subject instead, payload and headers as they arrived. On a JetStream consumer the delivery is then terminated, so the server delivers it no more. NATS has no dead-letter mechanism of its own, so the same path serves both models, and a warning names the subscription that gave up. The copy carries RETRY_COUNT_HEADER: on a Core subject it says how many deliveries the message had; on a JetStream consumer the server counted them, and the header reads 1. A cap without a dead-letter subject terminates the spent JetStream delivery, and ends the Core one. The dead-letter subject is an ordinary subject: a subscription of this service or of another one reads it. It stays outside every pattern a subscription of the service reads, or the spent message arrives back at a handler.

The dead-letter subject is read by an ordinary subscription. Macros Manual examples/nats_retry.rs /// The dead-letter subject is read by an ordinary subscription. The retry-count header says how /// many deliveries the payment had before it was carried here. #[subscriber("payments.dead")] async fn on_dead_letter(payment: &Payment, ctx: &mut Context<'_>) -> HandlerOutcome { let deliveries = ctx.headers().get_str(RETRY_COUNT_HEADER).unwrap_or("1"); tracing::error!(payment.id, deliveries, "payment dead-lettered"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } examples/manual/nats_retry.rs /// The dead-letter subject is read by an ordinary subscription. The retry-count header says how /// many deliveries the payment had before it was carried here. struct OnDeadLetter; impl Handle<Payment> for OnDeadLetter { fn handle( &self, payment: &Payment, _outs: &(), ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { let deliveries = ctx.headers().get_str(RETRY_COUNT_HEADER).unwrap_or("1"); tracing::error!(payment.id, deliveries, "payment dead-lettered"); ready(Ok(())) } }

A pattern names no subject of its own, so out_retry(Publish).to(subject) says where its delayed copies go; without it the app refuses to start. A CoreWildcard reads every subject its pattern matches, and a copy has to go to one of them. This crate does not take the pattern itself as a destination, so the mount site names the subject. A registration over a pattern that names no subject fails the start with an error naming the subscription. The service reports the gap at startup instead of losing every delayed message once it runs. out_retry binds the Retry slot, the one the framework publishes its copies through, to a policy; Publish is plain Core NATS. .to(subject) names the subject; a publish transform that declares Names can choose one per delivery instead. A subject the pattern matches brings the copy back to the same handler. The dead-letter subject stays outside the pattern, or the spent message comes back too. A CoreSubject and a JetStreamSubject name their own destination, so they need no out_retry; on them the slot only changes the policy or adds a transform.

Entries of every region are audited again a minute later through audits.retry, which the pattern reads. Macros Manual examples/nats_settlement_out_retry.rs /// Audits the entries of every region, `audits.eu`, `audits.us` and the rest. #[subscriber(CoreWildcard::new("audits.*"))] async fn audit(entry: &Entry) -> HandlerOutcome { if entry.posted { return HandlerOutcome::ack(); } tracing::info!(entry.id, "not posted yet, auditing again later"); HandlerOutcome::retry_after(RECHECK) } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("audit", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { // The copies go to "audits.retry", which the pattern reads, so they come back here. // The dead-letter subject is outside the pattern, so a spent entry does not. b.include(audit) .max_attempts(nonzero!(3u32)) .dead_letter("dead.audits") .out_retry(Publish) .to("audits.retry") }, ) } examples/manual/nats_settlement_out_retry.rs /// Audits the entries of every region, `audits.eu`, `audits.us` and the rest. struct Audit; impl Handle<Entry> for Audit { fn handle( &self, entry: &Entry, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { if entry.posted { return ready(Ok(())); } tracing::info!(entry.id, "not posted yet, auditing again later"); ready(Err(HandlerOutcome::retry_after(RECHECK))) } } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("audit", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { // The copies go to "audits.retry", which the pattern reads, so they come back here. // The dead-letter subject is outside the pattern, so a spent entry does not. b.include(subscriber(CoreWildcard::new("audits.*"), Audit).build()) .max_attempts(nonzero!(3u32)) .dead_letter("dead.audits") .out_retry(Publish) .to("audits.retry") }, ) }

max_attempts(n) caps the deliveries of one message; on JetStream it counts the server's own deliveries, on Core the copies in a header. It is declared at the mount site, and the first delivery counts as one. A JetStream consumer reports how many times it has delivered a message, so the cap reads that number. Every delivery counts: a retry, a retry_after, and a redelivery after ack_wait. A Core subject delivers each message once, so the framework counts the copies it publishes, in RETRY_COUNT_HEADER. Under a cap every retry on a Core subject travels as such a copy, an immediate one too. The delivery that reaches the cap goes to the dead-letter subject, or is terminated when the mount site names none. The cap is the framework's own: the consumer the crate creates leaves max_deliver at the server's default, unlimited, so the server delivers a retried message again until the cap ends it.

Five deliveries of one payment, on a Core subject and on a stream; the fifth that still fails goes to payments.dead. Macros Manual examples/nats_retry.rs #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("payments", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { // Five deliveries of one payment, the first included; the fifth that still fails goes // to "payments.dead" instead, payload and headers as they arrived. b.include(reconcile) .max_attempts(nonzero!(5u32)) .dead_letter("payments.dead") .include(store) .max_attempts(nonzero!(5u32)) .dead_letter("payments.dead") .include(on_dead_letter) }, ) } examples/manual/nats_retry.rs fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("payments", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { let stored = JetStreamSubject::new("payments.stored", "PAYMENTS").durable("reconciler"); // Five deliveries of one payment, the first included; the fifth that still fails goes // to "payments.dead" instead, payload and headers as they arrived. b.include(subscriber("payments.settled", Reconcile).build()) .max_attempts(nonzero!(5u32)) .dead_letter("payments.dead") .include(subscriber(stored, Reconcile).build()) .max_attempts(nonzero!(5u32)) .dead_letter("payments.dead") .include(subscriber("payments.dead", OnDeadLetter).build()) }, ) }

retry_after(delay) on JetStream puts the delay in the negative acknowledgement; on Core the framework publishes a copy after the delay. A JetStream consumer takes the delay as part of -NAK. The server holds the message for that long and delivers it again on the same consumer. Nothing is published, so the message keeps its stream sequence, and its delivery count rises by one. On a durable consumer the delayed message survives a restart of the service, because the server holds it. A Core subject has no acknowledgement to carry a delay. The framework waits out the delay in the service's memory and publishes a copy of the message, payload and headers, back to the subject the subscription reads. The copy carries RETRY_COUNT_HEADER, raised by one on every copy. A process that exits before the delay is over loses the copy. A CoreWildcard reads many subjects, so its mount site names where the copy goes with out_retry. A cap declared at the mount site ends the retries of one message.

A payment the ledger has not caught up with is checked again after 30 seconds, on a Core subject and on a stream. Macros Manual examples/nats_retry.rs /// The ledger has not caught up yet, so the delivery asks to come back later. On a Core subject /// the framework publishes a copy of the payment to the subject once the delay is over. #[subscriber("payments.settled")] async fn reconcile(payment: &Payment) -> HandlerOutcome { if payment.settled { return HandlerOutcome::ack(); } tracing::info!(payment.id, "not settled yet, checking again later"); HandlerOutcome::retry_after(RECHECK) } /// The same work through a stream: the delay rides the negative acknowledgement, and the server /// holds the message and delivers it again on this consumer. #[subscriber(JetStreamSubject::new("payments.stored", "PAYMENTS").durable("reconciler"))] async fn store(payment: &Payment) -> HandlerOutcome { if payment.settled { return HandlerOutcome::ack(); } tracing::info!(payment.id, "not settled yet, checking again later"); HandlerOutcome::retry_after(RECHECK) } examples/manual/nats_retry.rs /// The ledger has not caught up yet, so the delivery asks to come back later. Mounted on a Core /// subject, the framework publishes a copy of the payment to the subject once the delay is over; /// mounted on a stream consumer, the delay rides the negative acknowledgement and the server /// holds the message. struct Reconcile; impl Handle<Payment> for Reconcile { fn handle( &self, payment: &Payment, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { if payment.settled { return ready(Ok(())); } tracing::info!(payment.id, "not settled yet, checking again later"); ready(Err(HandlerOutcome::retry_after(RECHECK))) } }

A subject in #[subscriber] reads that Core NATS subject; a descriptor carries every other setting of its delivery model. #[subscriber("orders.created")] reads the subject orders.created over Core NATS, with no queue group. It is the same subscription as CoreSubject::new("orders.created"). Core NATS hands a message to whoever is subscribed at that moment and stores nothing, so a message published before the service starts never reaches it. Every other setting belongs to a descriptor, one type per delivery model: Descriptor Reads Its settings CoreSubject one Core NATS subject queue_group CoreWildcard every Core NATS subject a pattern matches queue_group JetStreamSubject a stream, through a pull consumer durable, filter_subject, deliver_policy, max_ack_pending, ack_wait, pull_expires A setting of the other model is not a method of the descriptor, so naming one does not compile. A descriptor goes where the subject goes, as the attribute's first argument. The manual form passes the subject, or the descriptor, to subscriber(source, body). The subscription's name is the subject the descriptor names: a test reads its deliveries under that name. All subscriptions of a service share the one connection of its NatsBroker.

The subject orders.created, read over Core NATS. Macros Manual examples/nats_subscriptions_name.rs /// Reads the Core NATS subject `orders.created`. #[subscriber("orders.created")] async fn place(order: &Order) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(order.id, "order placed"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")) .with_broker(NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { b.include(place) }) } examples/manual/nats_subscriptions_name.rs /// Reads the Core NATS subject `orders.created`. struct Place; impl Handle<Order> for Place { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(order.id, "order placed"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")) .with_broker(NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { b.include(subscriber("orders.created", Place).build()) }) }

A slice handler takes a batch: one JetStream pull fetch of the mount site's size, or a Core NATS batch the client assembles. A handler over &[T] is a batch handler, and batch(n) at the mount site is its largest batch. On a JetStreamSubject one batch is one pull request: the consumer asks the server for up to n messages. The fetch ends once it holds n, or once pull_expires runs out with fewer, 5 seconds by default. pull_expires takes a NonZeroDuration, because a fetch that expires at once would spin. Core NATS has no batch on the wire, so the client collects up to n deliveries and closes a short batch 10 ms after its first one. One outcome settles every message of the batch. A Vec<HandlerOutcome> settles message i with outcome i. In the manual form the body is an impl Handle<[T]>, where Ok(()) acknowledges the batch and Err(outcomes) settles message by message.

Three orders waiting in the stream arrive in one call. Macros Manual examples/nats_subscriptions_batches.rs /// Reconciles up to 50 orders per call; a fetch that finds fewer closes after 300 ms. #[subscriber( JetStreamSubject::new("orders.*", "ORDERS") .durable("reconciler") .pull_expires(NonZeroDuration::from_millis(nonzero!(300))) )] async fn reconcile(orders: &[Order]) -> HandlerOutcome { let total: u64 = orders.iter().map(|order| order.cents).sum(); tracing::info!(count = orders.len(), total, "orders reconciled"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("reconciliation", "0.1.0")) .with_broker(NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { b.include(reconcile.batch(nonzero!(50))) }) } examples/manual/nats_subscriptions_batches.rs /// Reconciles up to 50 orders per call; a fetch that finds fewer closes after 300 ms. struct Reconcile; impl Handle<[Order]> for Reconcile { fn handle( &self, orders: &[Order], _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), Vec<HandlerOutcome>>> { let total: u64 = orders.iter().map(|order| order.cents).sum(); tracing::info!(count = orders.len(), total, "orders reconciled"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("reconciliation", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { let orders = JetStreamSubject::new("orders.*", "ORDERS") .durable("reconciler") .pull_expires(NonZeroDuration::from_millis(nonzero!(300))); b.include(subscriber(orders, Reconcile).batch(nonzero!(50)).build()) }, ) }

CoreSubject reads one Core NATS subject; it stores nothing, and a delayed copy of a delivery is published back to the subject itself. CoreSubject::new takes the subject, and its one setting is the queue group. The server delivers a message to every subscription on the subject at that moment and keeps nothing for later. A subject is published to and subscribed to under one name, so a delayed retry needs nothing from the mount site. A retry_after(delay) settles the delivery, and after the delay the runtime publishes a copy back to the subject. The copy waits in the service's memory, so a process that exits before the timer fires loses it. A subject with * or > in it is a pattern, which is CoreWildcard; CoreSubject given one stops the service at startup. An empty subject stops it too. A stream that keeps messages for a consumer is JetStreamSubject.

A payment the bank has not cleared yet comes back to payments.captured after 30 seconds. Macros Manual examples/nats_subscriptions_core.rs /// Books a cleared payment; one the bank has not cleared yet comes back in 30 seconds, as a copy /// published to `payments.captured` again. #[subscriber(CoreSubject::new("payments.captured"))] async fn book(payment: &Payment) -> HandlerOutcome { if !payment.cleared { tracing::info!(payment.id, "not cleared yet, checking again later"); return HandlerOutcome::retry_after(RECHECK); } tracing::info!(payment.id, "payment booked"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("ledger", "0.1.0")) .with_broker(NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { b.include(book) }) } examples/manual/nats_subscriptions_core.rs /// Books a cleared payment; one the bank has not cleared yet comes back in 30 seconds, as a copy /// published to `payments.captured` again. struct Book; impl Handle<Payment> for Book { fn handle( &self, payment: &Payment, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { if !payment.cleared { tracing::info!(payment.id, "not cleared yet, checking again later"); return ready(Err(HandlerOutcome::retry_after(RECHECK))); } tracing::info!(payment.id, "payment booked"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("ledger", "0.1.0")) .with_broker(NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { b.include(subscriber(CoreSubject::new("payments.captured"), Book).build()) }) }

CoreWildcard reads every Core NATS subject a pattern matches, * for one token and > for the rest, and the mount site names where a delayed copy goes. A subject is a list of tokens separated by dots. orders.* matches orders.created and orders.cancelled, but not orders.eu.created. orders.> matches all three, and > alone matches every subject. CoreWildcard::new takes the pattern, and its one setting is the queue group. The subscription's name is the pattern itself. A pattern names many subjects and none of them in particular, so the crate does not choose where a delayed retry copy goes. The mount site names that subject with out_retry(Publish).to(subject). A registration over a pattern that names none stops the service at startup, with an error naming the subscription. A subject the pattern matches brings the copy back to the same handler.

Every one-token order event is audited, and a delayed copy goes to orders.audit. Macros Manual examples/nats_subscriptions_wildcard.rs /// Audits every one-token order event: `orders.created`, `orders.cancelled`, and the rest. #[subscriber(CoreWildcard::new("orders.*"))] async fn audit(event: &OrderEvent) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(event.order_id, "order event audited"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("audit", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { // A pattern is no destination, so the mount site names where a delayed copy goes. b.include(audit).out_retry(Publish).to("orders.audit") }, ) } examples/manual/nats_subscriptions_wildcard.rs /// Audits every one-token order event: `orders.created`, `orders.cancelled`, and the rest. struct Audit; impl Handle<OrderEvent> for Audit { fn handle( &self, event: &OrderEvent, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(event.order_id, "order event audited"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("audit", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { // A pattern is no destination, so the mount site names where a delayed copy goes. b.include(subscriber(CoreWildcard::new("orders.*"), Audit).build()) .out_retry(Publish) .to("orders.audit") }, ) }

DeliverPolicy says where a newly created consumer starts: all, new, last, last per subject, a sequence or a time. deliver_policy sets it on the descriptor. The type is the one async-nats defines, re-exported by the crate. All, the default, starts with the oldest message the stream holds. New starts with the first message published after the consumer was created. Last starts with the newest message of the stream, and LastPerSubject with the newest message of each subject the filter matches. ByStartSequence starts at a stream sequence, and ByStartTime at the first message stored at or after a time. The policy applies once, when the consumer is created. A durable consumer that already exists resumes from its own position. An ephemeral consumer is created on every startup, so it starts from its policy each time.

A live ticker starts with the next price, and the prices the stream held before it started stay behind. Macros Manual examples/nats_subscriptions_deliver.rs /// A live ticker: each new consumer starts with the next price, not with the stream's history. #[subscriber(JetStreamSubject::new("prices.*", "PRICES").deliver_policy(DeliverPolicy::New))] async fn tick(price: &Price) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(price.product, price.cents, "price changed"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("ticker", "0.1.0")) .with_broker(NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { b.include(tick) }) } examples/manual/nats_subscriptions_deliver.rs /// A live ticker: each new consumer starts with the next price, not with the stream's history. struct Tick; impl Handle<Price> for Tick { fn handle( &self, price: &Price, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(price.product, price.cents, "price changed"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn prices() -> JetStreamSubject { JetStreamSubject::new("prices.*", "PRICES").deliver_policy(DeliverPolicy::New) } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("ticker", "0.1.0")) .with_broker(NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { b.include(subscriber(prices(), Tick).build()) }) }

durable names a JetStream consumer: the server keeps its position across restarts, and subscriptions sharing it take messages in turn. A named consumer lives on the server, apart from any subscription. It remembers which messages were acknowledged, so a restarted service resumes after the last one and reads what arrived while it was down. A consumer without a name is ephemeral and starts from its deliver policy on every startup. Every replica of a service that reads through one durable shares its messages: each message goes to one of them, as in a queue group. At startup the subscription creates the consumer, or updates it when it exists. So the settings the last subscription opened with are the consumer's settings, and replicas that share a durable name one filter and one policy.

Every replica bills through the consumer billing, and a restarted service resumes where the consumer stopped. Macros Manual examples/nats_subscriptions_durable.rs /// Every replica reads through the consumer `billing`: each invoice is billed once, and a /// restarted service resumes where the consumer stopped. #[subscriber(JetStreamSubject::new("invoices.*", "INVOICES").durable("billing"))] async fn bill(invoice: &Invoice) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(invoice.id, "invoice billed"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("billing", "0.1.0")) .with_broker(NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { b.include(bill) }) } examples/manual/nats_subscriptions_durable.rs /// Every replica reads through the consumer `billing`: each invoice is billed once, and a /// restarted service resumes where the consumer stopped. struct Bill; impl Handle<Invoice> for Bill { fn handle( &self, invoice: &Invoice, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(invoice.id, "invoice billed"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("billing", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { let invoices = JetStreamSubject::new("invoices.*", "INVOICES").durable("billing"); b.include(subscriber(invoices, Bill).build()) }, ) }

filter_subject narrows the subjects of the stream a consumer reads; it defaults to the subject the descriptor names. A stream often stores several kinds of message under one prefix, such as every order event under orders.>. The consumer's filter decides which of them it is handed; the server skips the rest for this consumer. Without filter_subject the filter is the subject given to JetStreamSubject::new. With it, the descriptor's subject stays the subscription's name, and the filter decides what arrives. A filter may be a pattern with * and >. A durable consumer has one filter, the one its last subscription opened with.

The stream ORDERS stores every order event, and the refunds consumer reads orders.refunded only. Macros Manual examples/nats_subscriptions_filter.rs /// Reads only the refunds of the `ORDERS` stream, which stores every order event. #[subscriber( JetStreamSubject::new("orders.>", "ORDERS") .durable("refunds") .filter_subject("orders.refunded") )] async fn refund(order: &Order) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(order.id, "order refunded"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("refunds", "0.1.0")) .with_broker(NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { b.include(refund) }) } examples/manual/nats_subscriptions_filter.rs /// Reads only the refunds of the `ORDERS` stream, which stores every order event. struct Refund; impl Handle<Order> for Refund { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(order.id, "order refunded"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("refunds", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { let refunds = JetStreamSubject::new("orders.>", "ORDERS") .durable("refunds") .filter_subject("orders.refunded"); b.include(subscriber(refunds, Refund).build()) }, ) }

JetStreamSubject reads a stream through a pull consumer; the stream exists on the server before the service starts. A stream stores the messages published to its subjects, and a consumer reads them at its own pace. JetStreamSubject::new(subject, stream) takes the subject to read and the name of the stream that stores it. At startup the subscription finds the stream and creates its consumer; a stream the server does not have stops the service. The crate creates no stream: the service's deployment does, for example with nats stream add. Without durable the consumer is ephemeral, and the server discards it once the subscription closes. Each delivery settles on the server: an ack acknowledges it, and a retry or a delay is a negative acknowledgement the server acts on. The settings and their defaults: Setting Default What it does durable none, an ephemeral consumer names the consumer, which keeps its position across restarts filter_subject the subject narrows what the consumer reads from the stream deliver_policy DeliverPolicy::All where a new consumer starts max_ack_pending 1024 how many deliveries the consumer holds unacknowledged ack_wait 30 seconds how long the server waits for a settlement before it delivers again pull_expires 5 seconds how long one fetch of a batch waits for messages The subscription's name is the subject the descriptor names. A delivery carries its place in the stream, which a handler reads through the context keys.

The stream ORDERS stores orders.*, and an ephemeral consumer reads it. Macros Manual examples/nats_subscriptions_jetstream.rs /// Reads `orders.*` from the stream `ORDERS`; the ack settles each order on the server. #[subscriber(JetStreamSubject::new("orders.*", "ORDERS"))] async fn ship(order: &Order) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(order.id, "order shipped"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("shipping", "0.1.0")) .with_broker(NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { b.include(ship) }) } examples/manual/nats_subscriptions_jetstream.rs /// Reads `orders.*` from the stream `ORDERS`; `Ok` acknowledges each order on the server. struct Ship; impl Handle<Order> for Ship { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(order.id, "order shipped"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("shipping", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { let orders = JetStreamSubject::new("orders.*", "ORDERS"); b.include(subscriber(orders, Ship).build()) }, ) }

The nats-partition-key header keys the lanes of workers(n, by_key): messages sharing a key run on one lane, in order. workers(n, by_key) runs n sequential lanes in one subscription. Messages with one key run in order on one lane, and different keys run at once. NATS has no partitions or message keys, so the key travels in the nats-partition-key header. The sender sets it: any NATS client writes the header, and a RustStream message type declares it in its typed header contract. The value is text, because a NATS header is; a value that is not a single line of UTF-8 fails the publish. A message without the header has no key and rotates over the lanes. The lanes work the same on Core NATS and on a stream. The manual form writes the lanes as workers_by_key(n) on the mount chain.

Two tenants' orders, each order a second of work: the tenants run side by side, two seconds in all. Macros Manual examples/nats_subscriptions_keys.rs /// Eight lanes keyed by the partition-key header: one tenant's orders run in order, different /// tenants at once. #[subscriber(CoreSubject::new("orders.placed"), workers(8, by_key))] async fn place(order: &Order) -> HandlerOutcome { process(order).await; HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")) .with_broker(NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { b.include(place) }) } examples/manual/nats_subscriptions_keys.rs /// Eight lanes keyed by the partition-key header: one tenant's orders run in order, different /// tenants at once. struct Place; impl Handle<Order> for Place { async fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> Result<(), HandlerOutcome> { process(order).await; Ok(()) } } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { let placed = CoreSubject::new("orders.placed"); b.include( subscriber(placed, Place) .workers_by_key(nonzero!(8)) .build(), ) }, ) }

max_ack_pending caps how many unacknowledged deliveries the server lets a consumer hold at once; the default is 1024. A delivery is pending from the moment the server hands it out until it is settled. Once the consumer holds that many, the server stops delivering until a settlement frees a place. The cap belongs to the consumer, so every subscription that shares a durable counts against one cap. It bounds the work in flight from the server's side, whatever the service does. workers(n) runs up to n handlers at once in one subscription; with a cap below n, the cap is the limit. A delivery the consumer holds counts against its ack_wait from the moment it is handed out, so a large cap over slow handlers lets deliveries wait out their ack_wait and come back. The cap is enforced by the server, so a test of it runs against a live server.

Six workers render reports, and the server hands out two at a time. Macros Manual examples/nats_subscriptions_pending.rs /// Six workers, but the server hands out at most two reports before they are acknowledged, so /// two render at a time. #[subscriber( JetStreamSubject::new("reports.requested", "REPORTS") .durable("renderers") .max_ack_pending(2), workers(6) )] async fn produce(report: &Report) -> HandlerOutcome { render(report).await; HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("reports", "0.1.0")) .with_broker(NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { b.include(produce) }) } examples/manual/nats_subscriptions_pending.rs /// Six workers, but the server hands out at most two reports before they are acknowledged, so /// two render at a time. struct Produce; impl Handle<Report> for Produce { async fn handle( &self, report: &Report, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> Result<(), HandlerOutcome> { render(report).await; Ok(()) } } fn reports() -> JetStreamSubject { JetStreamSubject::new("reports.requested", "REPORTS") .durable("renderers") .max_ack_pending(2) } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("reports", "0.1.0")) .with_broker(NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { b.include(subscriber(reports(), Produce).workers(nonzero!(6)).build()) }) }

queue_group puts a Core NATS subscription in a queue group: each message goes to one member, and one name is one group across subjects. Without a group, every subscription on a subject receives every message. Replicas of a service that subscribe in one group share the messages instead, and the server picks one member for each. A subscription outside the group still receives everything, so an audit can read beside the workers. The server keys a group by its name alone, so subscriptions with one group name on two subjects or patterns are one group. A message both of them match is delivered once, to one member. CoreSubject::queue_group and CoreWildcard::queue_group take the same name. Core NATS keeps nothing for a group: a message published while no member is subscribed is lost. On a stream the same sharing comes from a durable consumer that several subscriptions read through.

Every replica fulfils orders in the group fulfilment, and the audit reads every order outside it. Macros Manual examples/nats_subscriptions_queue.rs /// Every replica of the service joins `fulfilment`, so each order is fulfilled once. #[subscriber(CoreSubject::new("orders.created").queue_group("fulfilment"))] async fn fulfil(order: &Order) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(order.id, "order fulfilled"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } /// Outside the group: the audit reads every order. #[subscriber(CoreWildcard::new("orders.*"))] async fn audit(order: &Order) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(order.id, "order audited"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("fulfilment", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { b.include(fulfil) .include(audit) .out_retry(Publish) .to("orders.audit") }, ) } examples/manual/nats_subscriptions_queue.rs /// Every replica of the service joins `fulfilment`, so each order is fulfilled once. struct Fulfil; impl Handle<Order> for Fulfil { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(order.id, "order fulfilled"); ready(Ok(())) } } /// Outside the group: the audit reads every order. struct Audit; impl Handle<Order> for Audit { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(order.id, "order audited"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("fulfilment", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { let fulfilment = CoreSubject::new("orders.created").queue_group("fulfilment"); b.include(subscriber(fulfilment, Fulfil).build()) .include(subscriber(CoreWildcard::new("orders.*"), Audit).build()) .out_retry(Publish) .to("orders.audit") }, ) }

TestApp::start connects NatsBroker in process: subjects, queue groups, streams, consumers and request-reply, with no server. A test hands the harness the app main runs, unchanged, and addresses the broker by its production type, tb.broker::<NatsBroker>(). The testing feature in [dev-dependencies] adds the in-process mode, and turns on the core's harness with it. The in-process mode has no settings of its own. It parses the addresses as the client parses them, so an address the client refuses fails TestApp::start. It reads the two connection options that change what the server delivers, no_echo and the inbox prefix. It routes as a server routes. A Core NATS subscription receives every subject its subject or pattern matches, and a queue group hands each message to one of its members. A stream stores what its consumers' filter subjects place in it, and a stream a subscription names is there for it. A consumer starts where its deliver policy says, numbers its deliveries, and fills every key of the JetStream context. A JetStream delivery is acknowledged, redelivered, terminated or held for a delay as on a server, and one left unsettled comes back after its ack_wait. A Core NATS delivery has no acknowledgement and is never redelivered. A request to a subject nobody reads fails at once with "no responders". It refuses what a server refuses: a subject with whitespace, a header with no NATS form, a message over the 1 MiB payload limit, a JetStream publish no stream stores, an expectation that does not hold, and every publish after the broker shut down. What only a server has is for a live test: a stream's own subject list and limits, a stream the server lacks, max_ack_pending, authentication and TLS, and the connect itself. A publish through the harness returns once every handler it woke has settled, a reply included. The assertions that follow read finished state.

The dependency line: [dev-dependencies] ruststream-nats = { version = "0.8", features = ["testing"] } The tests publish a payment and read how the handler settled it. TestApp::start_live runs the same test body against a running NATS server, for what only a server has. It connects the broker through its ordinary connect, so startup dials the server and every JetStream subscription looks up its stream there. The body is the one an in-process test runs; only the start call differs. A publish, settle and advance wait on the real clock until every subscription has handled what was published to it. The wait lasts ten seconds at most, and start_live_within sets another bound. The live mode is for what the in-process mode leaves to the server: a stream's own subject list and limits, a stream the server lacks failing startup, max_ack_pending, authentication and TLS, and the timing of the connect. A stream is the server's state, and the server keeps what earlier runs left in it. So a test creates the stream through an admin connection's jetstream before the app starts, replacing a leftover, and deletes it afterwards. In the example, live::url returns the server's address from NATS_TEST_URL, and the test returns early without one, so cargo test passes on a machine with no server. A job that stood a server up sets RUSTSTREAM_REQUIRE_LIVE=1, and a missing address then fails the test instead of skipping it. The repository's stand is docker-compose.test.yml, a NATS server with JetStream that just brokers-up starts.

The two tests share one body: one in process, one against the server at NATS_TEST_URL. 本指南用处理器的结果结算 JetStream 投递，为慢处理器设定 ack_wait，处理投递了两次的消息，并说明 Core NATS 不保证什么。 处理器用它返回的值结算自己的投递，运行时在处理器结束后发送结算。 在 JetStream 消费者上，每种结果都是一个服务器据以行动的确认： 结果 发给服务器 服务器做什么 ack +ACK 这个消费者不再保留这条消息 retry -NAK 立即再次投递它 retry_after(delay) 带延迟的 -NAK 扣留它，延迟过后再次投递 drop +TERM 不再投递它 没有结算 什么也不发 ack_wait 过后再次投递它 重新投递保留消息的流序号，服务器统计它的投递次数。 示例是一个支付服务。 它通过银行扣收已授权的付款，并把每次扣款通知给看板。

宏 手写 src/main.rs /// How long a busy bank asks its callers to wait. const BACKOFF: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30); #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, Outgoing)] #[outgoing(name = "payments.authorized")] struct Payment { id: u64, card: String, amount_cents: u64, } #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, Outgoing)] #[outgoing(name = "payments.captured")] struct Captured { payment: u64, amount_cents: u64, } #[subscriber( JetStreamSubject::new("payments.authorized", "PAYMENTS") .durable("capture") .ack_wait(NonZeroDuration::from_secs(nonzero!(60))), reply )] async fn capture( payment: &Payment, Ctx(delivered): Ctx<Delivered>, State(bank): State<Arc<Bank>>, ) -> Result<Captured, HandlerOutcome> { if delivered.is_some_and(|count| count > 1) { tracing::info!(payment.id, ?delivered, "payment delivered again"); } match bank.capture(payment).await { Ok(()) => Ok(Captured { payment: payment.id, amount_cents: payment.amount_cents, }), // Past the rate limit: the server holds the payment and delivers it after the delay. Err(Refusal::Busy) => Err(HandlerOutcome::retry_after(BACKOFF)), // No answer: the server delivers the payment again at once. Err(Refusal::Unavailable) => Err(HandlerOutcome::retry()), // The server never delivers a terminated payment again. Err(Refusal::Declined) => { tracing::warn!(payment.id, "card declined, payment terminated"); Err(HandlerOutcome::drop()) } } } src/main.rs /// How long a busy bank asks its callers to wait. const BACKOFF: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30); #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)] #[schemars(crate = "ruststream::schemars")] struct Payment { id: u64, card: String, amount_cents: u64, } impl OutgoingDestination for Payment { type Form = FixedName; const DESTINATION: &'static str = "payments.authorized"; } impl MessageHeaders for Payment { type Contract = NoHeaders; } impl MessageInfo for Payment { const NAME: &'static str = "Payment"; } #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)] #[schemars(crate = "ruststream::schemars")] struct Captured { payment: u64, amount_cents: u64, } impl OutgoingDestination for Captured { type Form = FixedName; const DESTINATION: &'static str = "payments.captured"; } impl MessageHeaders for Captured { type Contract = NoHeaders; } impl MessageInfo for Captured { const NAME: &'static str = "Captured"; } struct Capture; impl Handle<Payment, Captured, (), JetStreamContext, Clients> for Capture { async fn handle( &self, payment: &Payment, _outs: &(), ctx: &mut Context<'_, JetStreamContext, Clients>, ) -> Result<Captured, HandlerOutcome> { let delivered = ctx.context(DELIVERED); if delivered.is_some_and(|count| count > 1) { tracing::info!(payment.id, ?delivered, "payment delivered again"); } match ctx.state().bank.capture(payment).await { Ok(()) => Ok(Captured { payment: payment.id, amount_cents: payment.amount_cents, }), // Past the rate limit: the server holds the payment and delivers it after the delay. Err(Refusal::Busy) => Err(HandlerOutcome::retry_after(BACKOFF)), // No answer: the server delivers the payment again at once. Err(Refusal::Unavailable) => Err(HandlerOutcome::retry()), // The server never delivers a terminated payment again. Err(Refusal::Declined) => { tracing::warn!(payment.id, "card declined, payment terminated"); Err(HandlerOutcome::drop()) } } } } 银行有四种答复，每种需要不同的结果。 扣款成功时返回 Captured，运行时把它作为回复发布，然后确认这笔付款。 Busy 表示银行的速率限额已经用完，所以付款在服务器上等待 30 秒。 Unavailable 表示银行没有应答，所以付款立即回来。 Declined 表示这张卡无法扣款，再试一次也是同样的答复，所以这笔付款被终止。 不设上限的 retry 会无休止地回来；重试与死信加上上限和死信 subject。
JetStream 至少投递一次。 在 retry 之后、ack_wait 耗尽之后，以及进程在结算前停止之后，付款都会回来。 所以处理器会两次看到某些付款，它的工作必须能接受重复。 这里银行把付款 id 当作幂等键，重复的扣款只扣一次。 Ctx<Delivered> 是服务器统计的投递次数，第一次投递时为 1；capture 会记录它再次看到的付款。
服务器等待结算的时间是 ack_wait，描述符未另行指定时为 30 秒。 超时后它再次投递消息，而第一个处理器可能仍在运行。 capture 设为 60 秒，高于银行答复的最长时间。 把 ack_wait 设得高于处理器的最坏耗时，两次投递就永远不会重叠。 耗尽的 ack_wait 也计入尝试上限的投递次数。

宏 手写 src/main.rs #[subscriber("payments.captured")] async fn refresh(captured: &Captured) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(captured.payment, "dashboard refreshed"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } src/main.rs struct Refresh; impl Handle<Captured, (), (), (), Clients> for Refresh { fn handle( &self, captured: &Captured, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_, (), Clients>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(captured.payment, "dashboard refreshed"); ready(Ok(())) } } refresh 从一个 Core NATS subject 读取扣款。 Core NATS 至多投递一次，并且没有确认。 结算 Core 投递会报告 AckError::Unsupported，运行时把它记录为警告。 进程丢失的 Core 消息就此消失，没有任何东西能把它找回来。 看板可以丢失一次更新，因为下一次扣款会再次刷新它。 付款不能丢失，所以付款经由流传递。

宏 手写 src/main.rs #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App<State = Clients> { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("payments", "0.1.0")) .on_startup(async move |()| Ok::<_, Infallible>(Clients::default())) .with_broker(NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { b.include(capture).include(refresh) }) } src/main.rs fn app() -> impl App<State = Clients> { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("payments", "0.1.0")) .on_startup(async move |()| Ok::<_, Infallible>(Clients::default())) .with_broker(NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { b.include( subscriber( JetStreamSubject::new("payments.authorized", "PAYMENTS") .durable("capture") .ack_wait(NonZeroDuration::from_secs(nonzero!(60))), Capture, ) .reply() .build(), ) .include(subscriber("payments.captured", Refresh).build()) }) } fn main() -> ExitCode { run_main(app) } 银行客户端是应用的状态，在启动时打开一次。 批处理器用一个结果结算整批；返回 Vec<HandlerOutcome> 时，则逐条结算每条消息。 示例文件中的测试在暂停的时钟上于进程内运行应用，所以 Busy 的 30 秒瞬间就过去了。
本指南安装 ruststream-nats，启动一个本地 NATS 服务器，并让第一个服务连上它运行。

Cargo.toml [dependencies] ruststream = { version = "0.8", features = ["macros", "json", "logging"] } ruststream-nats = "0.8" serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] } tracing = "0.1" [dev-dependencies] ruststream-nats = { version = "0.8", features = ["testing"] } tokio = { version = "1", features = ["macros", "rt"] } ruststream 是框架本身：macros 提供属性宏，json 提供默认编解码器，logging 把服务的日志打印到终端。 ruststream-nats 是 NATS Broker。 它的 testing feature 加入测试所用的进程内 NATS。 这个 Broker crate 有两个 feature，默认都不开启： Feature 提供的内容 testing TestApp 背后的进程内 NATS asyncapi 生成的 AsyncAPI 文档中的 NATS 绑定 底层客户端是 async-nats。 它用 Rust 编写，通过 rustls 实现 TLS，所以构建不需要任何系统库。

开发时，一个开启了 JetStream 的 NATS 服务器就够了： compose.yaml services: nats: image: nats:2-alpine command: ["-js"] ports: - "4222:4222" docker compose up -d 服务器监听 localhost:4222。 -js 开启 JetStream，即从流与消费者开始的各篇指南所读写的流。 示例用 NATS 命令行工具 nats 发布消息。

生产集群有多台服务器，会要求服务表明身份，并且使用 TLS 通信。 这些都是 async-nats ConnectOptions 的设置，Broker 在发起任何连接之前接收它。

src/main.rs /// Where the cluster is and who the service is, as the deployment provides them. struct Deployment { /// One server address or a comma-separated list. servers: String, /// The contents of the service's `.creds` file: its user JWT and its `NKey` seed. creds: String, /// The certificate authority that signed the servers' certificates. ca: PathBuf, } impl Deployment { fn from_env() -> io::Result<Self> { let var = |name: &str| { env::var(name).map_err(|_| io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::NotFound, name.to_owned())) }; Ok(Self { servers: var("NATS_SERVERS")?, creds: fs::read_to_string(var("NATS_CREDS")?)?, ca: var("NATS_CA")?.into(), }) } } fn broker(deployment: Deployment) -> io::Result<NatsBroker> { let options = ConnectOptions::with_credentials(&deployment.creds)? .add_root_certificates(deployment.ca) .require_tls(true) .name("orders") .connection_timeout(Duration::from_secs(10)); Ok(NatsBroker::new(deployment.servers).with_options(options)) } Cargo.toml [dependencies] async-nats = "0.50" 部署环境通过环境变量提供服务器地址和两个文件路径。 NatsBroker::new 接收一个地址或以逗号分隔的地址列表，客户端从中选一个去连接。 with_options 附加 ConnectOptions，此时仍不发起任何连接。 .creds 文件保存用户 JWT 及其 NKey 种子，Synadia Cloud 和用 nsc 配置的账户就是这样识别服务的。 应用读取这个文件，把内容交给 ConnectOptions::with_credentials，后者立即解析它。 ConnectOptions::with_credentials_file 会自己读取文件，但它是 async 的，而应用是在同步函数中构建的。 无法解析的文件会让服务在连接之前就停止。 服务器配置了用户名和密码时，使用 ConnectOptions::with_user_and_password；配置了令牌时使用 with_token；只配置了 NKey 时使用 with_nkey。 add_root_certificates 指定为服务器证书签名的证书颁发机构，require_tls 拒绝不使用 TLS 的连接。 集群要求双向 TLS 时，add_client_certificate 加入服务自己的证书。 客户端在连接时读取证书文件。 name 让服务显示在服务器的监控中，connection_timeout 限制每次连接尝试的时间。

}; let request = OutgoingMessage::new("prices.quote", ask.as_slice()); let reply = match pricing.request(request, PRICING_TIMEOUT).await { Ok(reply) => reply, Err(err) => { tracing::warn!(order.id, %err, "no price, the order asks again later"); return Err(HandlerOutcome::retry_after(RETRY_DELAY)); } }; let Ok(price) = serde_json::from_slice::<Price>(reply.payload()) else { return Err(HandlerOutcome::drop()); }; tracing::info!(order.id, price.cents, "order priced"); Ok(Priced { order: order.id, cents: price.cents, }) } src/main.rs /// How long the orders service waits for a price. const PRICING_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(2); /// How long an order waits before it asks for its price again. const RETRY_DELAY: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30); #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)] #[schemars(crate = "ruststream::schemars")] struct Order { id: u64, sku: String, } impl OutgoingDestination for Order { type Form = FixedName; const DESTINATION: &'static str = "orders.placed"; } impl MessageHeaders for Order { type Contract = NoHeaders; } impl MessageInfo for Order { const NAME: &'static str = "Order"; } #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)] #[schemars(crate = "ruststream::schemars")] struct Priced { order: u64, cents: u64, } impl OutgoingDestination for Priced { type Form = FixedName; const DESTINATION: &'static str = "orders.priced"; } impl MessageHeaders for Priced { type Contract = NoHeaders; } impl MessageInfo for Priced { const NAME: &'static str = "Priced"; } struct Pricing; impl OutSlot for Pricing { const NAME: &'static str = "Pricing"; type Destination = Reads; } struct PriceOrder; impl<Asks> Handle<Order, Priced, Outs<(Asks,)>> for PriceOrder where Asks: OutEntry<Pricing, Wire: RequestReply>, { async fn handle( &self, order: &Order, outs: &Outs<(Asks,)>, _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> Result<Priced, HandlerOutcome> { let Ok(ask) = serde_json::to_vec(&Ask { sku: order.sku.clone(), }) else { return Err(HandlerOutcome::drop()); }; let request = OutgoingMessage::new("prices.quote", ask.as_slice()); let reply = match outs.get(Pricing).request(request, PRICING_TIMEOUT).await { Ok(reply) => reply, Err(err) => { tracing::warn!(order.id, %err, "no price, the order asks again later"); return Err(HandlerOutcome::retry_after(RETRY_DELAY)); } }; let Ok(price) = serde_json::from_slice::<Price>(reply.payload()) else { return Err(HandlerOutcome::drop()); }; tracing::info!(order.id, price.cents, "order priced"); Ok(Priced { order: order.id, cents: price.cents, }) } } price_order 从一个流读取新订单，并在 prices.quote 上询问每个订单的价格。 Pricing 槽位的约束是 Out<impl RequestReply, _>：主体说明它需要请求-应答，但不指名任何 Broker。 应用把这个槽位与普通的 Publish 策略配对，在 NATS 上，该策略的发布者具备请求-应答能力。 request 用一个新的 inbox 发布问题，并以其上的第一条消息作为结果。 问题是一条原始消息，所以主体自己编码问题、解码应答，这里用的是 serde_json。 价格确定后，订单的回复 Priced 随即发出。 请求有两种失败方式。 没有任何订阅读取该 subject 时，服务器立即以 "no responders" 应答。 响应方存在却一直沉默时，请求在超时后返回 NatsError::RequestTimeout 错误，这里的超时是两秒。 无论哪种情况，订单都在流上等待 30 秒，然后再问一次。

宏 手写 src/main.rs #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App<State = ()> { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { b.include(quote) .out(Answers, Publish) .include(price_order) .out_reply(Publish) .out(Pricing, Publish) }, ) } src/main.rs fn app() -> impl App<State = ()> { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { b.include( subscriber( CoreSubject::new("prices.quote").queue_group("pricing"), Quote, ) .build(), ) .out(Answers, Publish) .include( subscriber( JetStreamSubject::new("orders.placed", "ORDERS").durable("pricer"), PriceOrder, ) .reply() .build(), ) .out_reply(Publish) .out(Pricing, Publish) }, ) } fn main() -> ExitCode { run_main(app) } 两个槽位都使用普通的 Publish 策略：一个发布应答，另一个提出问题。 启动钩子也以同样的方式提问：调用 b.after_startup(Publish, ..)，在交给它的发布者上调用 request。 示例文件中的测试在进程内的一个应用中运行这两部分。 进程内 NATS 把请求路由到应用自己的响应方，在没有订阅读取该 subject 时应答 "no responders"，并让沉默的响应方超时。

本指南立即或稍后重试一次投递，限定尝试次数，并把一直失败的消息存入死信流，适用于流消费者、Core subject 和模式。 NATS 没有死信机制。 JetStream 可以限定一条消息的投递次数，但不会把最后一次投递发往任何地方。 因此由挂载点声明上限和死信 subject，框架把它们应用到两种模型上。 示例是一个支付服务，它通过银行结清付款并发出退款。 它把死信保存在一个专用的流中： nats stream add PAYMENTS --subjects 'payments.settle' --defaults nats stream add DEAD --subjects 'dead.*' --defaults

宏 手写 src/main.rs /// How long a busy bank asks its callers to wait. const BACKOFF: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30); /// The outcome a refusal of the bank calls for. fn outcome(refusal: Refusal) -> HandlerOutcome { match refusal { // Past the rate limit: a call right now would be refused again. Refusal::Busy => HandlerOutcome::retry_after(BACKOFF), // No answer: try again at once, up to the attempt cap. Refusal::Unavailable => HandlerOutcome::retry(), Refusal::Declined => HandlerOutcome::drop(), } } #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, Outgoing)] #[outgoing(name = "payments.settle")] struct Payment { id: u64, card: String, amount_cents: u64, } #[subscriber(JetStreamSubject::new("payments.settle", "PAYMENTS").durable("settler"))] async fn settle(payment: &Payment, State(bank): State<Arc<Bank>>) -> HandlerOutcome { match bank.charge(&payment.card).await { Ok(()) => HandlerOutcome::ack(), Err(refusal) => { tracing::warn!(payment.id, ?refusal, "payment refused by the bank"); outcome(refusal) } } } src/main.rs /// How long a busy bank asks its callers to wait. const BACKOFF: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30); /// The outcome a refusal of the bank calls for. fn outcome(refusal: Refusal) -> HandlerOutcome { match refusal { // Past the rate limit: a call right now would be refused again. Refusal::Busy => HandlerOutcome::retry_after(BACKOFF), // No answer: try again at once, up to the attempt cap. Refusal::Unavailable => HandlerOutcome::retry(), Refusal::Declined => HandlerOutcome::drop(), } } #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)] #[schemars(crate = "ruststream::schemars")] struct Payment { id: u64, card: String, amount_cents: u64, } impl OutgoingDestination for Payment { type Form = FixedName; const DESTINATION: &'static str = "payments.settle"; } impl MessageHeaders for Payment { type Contract = NoHeaders; } impl MessageInfo for Payment { const NAME: &'static str = "Payment"; } struct Settle; impl Handle<Payment, (), (), (), Clients> for Settle { async fn handle( &self, payment: &Payment, _outs: &(), ctx: &mut Context<'_, (), Clients>, ) -> Result<(), HandlerOutcome> { match ctx.state().bank.charge(&payment.card).await { Ok(()) => Ok(()), Err(refusal) => { tracing::warn!(payment.id, ?refusal, "payment refused by the bank"); Err(outcome(refusal)) } } } } outcome 把银行的拒绝变成处理器的结果。 银行繁忙时，retry_after 在 30 秒后再问一次。 在 JetStream 消费者上，延迟放在否定确认里：服务器扣留这笔付款，然后在同一个消费者上以相同的流序号再次投递它。 不发布任何东西，在此期间停止的进程也不会丢失任何东西。 银行没有应答时，retry 立即再问一次；卡被拒时，付款被丢弃。

宏 手写 src/main.rs #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App<State = Clients> { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("payments", "0.1.0")) .on_startup(async move |()| Ok::<_, Infallible>(Clients::default())) .with_broker(NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { // Five deliveries of one payment, the first included; then the dead-letter subject. b.include(settle) .max_attempts(nonzero!(5u32)) .dead_letter("dead.payments") .include(review) // A pattern is no subject to publish a copy to, so the mount site names one. .include(send_refund) .max_attempts(nonzero!(3u32)) .dead_letter("dead.refunds") .out_retry(Publish) .to("refunds.retry") }) } src/main.rs fn app() -> impl App<State = Clients> { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("payments", "0.1.0")) .on_startup(async move |()| Ok::<_, Infallible>(Clients::default())) .with_broker(NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { b.include( subscriber( JetStreamSubject::new("payments.settle", "PAYMENTS").durable("settler"), Settle, ) .build(), ) // Five deliveries of one payment, the first included; then the dead-letter subject. .max_attempts(nonzero!(5u32)) .dead_letter("dead.payments") .include( subscriber( JetStreamSubject::new("dead.payments", "DEAD").durable("review"), Review, ) .build(), ) // A pattern is no subject to publish a copy to, so the mount site names one. .include(subscriber(CoreWildcard::new("refunds.*"), SendRefund).build()) .max_attempts(nonzero!(3u32)) .dead_letter("dead.refunds") .out_retry(Publish) .to("refunds.retry") }) } fn main() -> ExitCode { run_main(app) } max_attempts 统计一笔付款的每次投递，第一次也算在内。 在 JetStream 消费者上，这个次数就是服务器自己统计的次数，所以耗尽的 ack_wait 也计算在内。 第五次投递不再重试：dead_letter 把它发布到 dead.payments，载荷和消息头保持到达时的样子。 被丢弃的付款完成结算，不会去任何地方，所以死信中只有用完了尝试次数的付款。 设了上限却没有死信 subject 的消费者，会终止它的最后一次投递。 dead.payments 是一次普通发布，而 Core NATS 不保存无人读取的消息。 DEAD 流保存它，所以死信会一直等到有人查看。 应用读取的任何 subject 都不与死信 subject 匹配，否则用完尝试次数的投递会回到放弃了它的处理器。

宏 手写 src/main.rs #[subscriber(JetStreamSubject::new("dead.payments", "DEAD").durable("review"))] async fn review(payment: &Payment) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::error!(payment.id, "payment needs a person to look at it"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } src/main.rs struct Review; impl Handle<Payment, (), (), (), Clients> for Review { fn handle( &self, payment: &Payment, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_, (), Clients>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::error!(payment.id, "payment needs a person to look at it"); ready(Ok(())) } } review 像读取其他流一样从 DEAD 流读取失败的付款，并把每一笔记入日志，留给人来查看。

宏 手写 src/main.rs #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, Outgoing)] struct Refund { id: u64, card: String, amount_cents: u64, } #[subscriber(CoreWildcard::new("refunds.*"))] async fn send_refund(refund: &Refund, State(bank): State<Arc<Bank>>) -> HandlerOutcome { match bank.charge(&refund.card).await { Ok(()) => HandlerOutcome::ack(), Err(refusal) => { tracing::warn!(refund.id, ?refusal, "refund refused by the bank"); outcome(refusal) } } } src/main.rs #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)] #[schemars(crate = "ruststream::schemars")] struct Refund { id: u64, card: String, amount_cents: u64, } impl OutgoingDestination for Refund { type Form = CallerName; } impl MessageHeaders for Refund { type Contract = NoHeaders; } impl MessageInfo for Refund { const NAME: &'static str = "Refund"; } struct SendRefund; impl Handle<Refund, (), (), (), Clients> for SendRefund { async fn handle( &self, refund: &Refund, _outs: &(), ctx: &mut Context<'_, (), Clients>, ) -> Result<(), HandlerOutcome> { match ctx.state().bank.charge(&refund.card).await { Ok(()) => Ok(()), Err(refusal) => { tracing::warn!(refund.id, ?refusal, "refund refused by the bank"); Err(outcome(refusal)) } } } } Core NATS 无法扣留消息。 在 Core 订阅上，一次重试就是框架发布的投递副本：retry 立即发布它，retry_after 在延迟结束时发布它。 副本在 x-ruststream-retry-count 消息头中带着投递次数，上限读取的就是它。 延迟的副本是至多一次的：在延迟结束前停止的进程会丢失它。 CoreSubject 把副本发布到它自己的 subject。 send_refund 读取模式 refunds.*，这个模式没有唯一的 subject 可供发布。 所以应用用 out_retry(Publish).to("refunds.retry") 指定一个模式能匹配的 subject，副本就会回到 send_refund。 基于模式却没有这一设置的注册拒绝启动，不论它的处理器是否重试。 退款的第三次投递进入 dead.refunds，次数记在消息头里。 示例文件中的测试在暂停的时钟上于进程内运行应用，所以 tb.advance(BACKOFF) 让 30 秒瞬间过去。 测试 NATS 服务讲解了测试套件。
documents.s: 在 Core subject 上重试

documents.t: 本指南通过持久化消费者和临时消费者读取 JetStream 流，选择新消费者从哪里开始，读取投递的元数据，并成批接收消息。 流保存发布到它的 subject 上的消息，每条消息都有一个序号。 消费者按自己的节奏读取流，并逐条确认消息。 示例是一个网店。 它履行新订单，在看板上显示每个订单事件，并与银行核对已付款的订单。

流是服务器的状态。 服务在启动时查找它，从不创建它，所以要用 NATS 命令行工具创建一次： nats stream add ORDERS --subjects 'orders.*' --defaults ORDERS 保存发布到 orders.created、orders.paid 以及 orders.* 匹配的其他任何 subject 上的每条消息。 向这样的 subject 做一次普通发布，消息就会被保存，不论发布者是谁。 订阅服务器上不存在的流，会让服务启动失败。

宏 手写 src/main.rs /// What the warehouse is asked to ship. The sequence is the order's place in the stream. #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, Outgoing)] #[outgoing(name = "shipments.requested")] struct Shipment { order: u64, sequence: Option<u64>, } #[subscriber( JetStreamSubject::new("orders.created", "ORDERS").durable("fulfilment"), reply )] async fn fulfil(order: &Order, Ctx(sequence): Ctx<StreamSequence>) -> Shipment { tracing::info!(order.id, ?sequence, "order sent to the warehouse"); Shipment { order: order.id, sequence, } } src/main.rs /// What the warehouse is asked to ship. The sequence is the order's place in the stream. #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)] #[schemars(crate = "ruststream::schemars")] struct Shipment { order: u64, sequence: Option<u64>, } impl OutgoingDestination for Shipment { type Form = FixedName; const DESTINATION: &'static str = "shipments.requested"; } impl MessageHeaders for Shipment { type Contract = NoHeaders; } impl MessageInfo for Shipment { const NAME: &'static str = "Shipment"; } struct Fulfil; impl Handle<Order, Shipment, (), JetStreamContext> for Fulfil { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), ctx: &mut Context<'_, JetStreamContext>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<Shipment, HandlerOutcome>> { let sequence = ctx.context(STREAM_SEQUENCE); tracing::info!(order.id, ?sequence, "order sent to the warehouse"); ready(Ok(Shipment { order: order.id, sequence, })) } } JetStreamSubject 接收消费者读取的 subject 和保存它的流。 subject 就是消费者的过滤条件，所以 fulfil 只从 ORDERS 中读取 orders.created。 两者需要不同时，filter_subject 设置另一个过滤条件。 服务在启动时创建消费者，带上描述符的每一项设置。 durable 把消费者命名为 fulfilment。 服务器保存它的位置，所以重启后的服务从停下的地方继续。 服务的各个副本共用这一个持久化消费者，每条消息交给其中一个副本。 这就是 JetStream 中与队列组相对应的机制。 处理器用 Ctx<StreamSequence> 读取投递在流中的位置。 JetStream 上下文还带有流和消费者的名字、消费者序号、投递次数，以及仍在等待的消息数。 在手写形式中，处理器接收 Context<'_, JetStreamContext>，用 ctx.context(..) 读取同样的键。 在 Core NATS 投递上，每个键读出的都是 None。

宏 手写 src/main.rs #[subscriber(JetStreamSubject::new("orders.*", "ORDERS").deliver_policy(DeliverPolicy::New))] async fn show(order: &Order) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(order.id, "order event on the dashboard"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } src/main.rs struct Show; impl Handle<Order> for Show { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(order.id, "order event on the dashboard"); ready(Ok(())) } } 没有 durable 的描述符创建一个临时消费者。 每个进程得到自己的消费者，订阅关闭后服务器删除它。 所以服务的每个副本都显示每个订单事件。 DeliverPolicy 决定新消费者从哪里开始。 默认的 All 从流保存的第一条消息开始，New 从下一条发布的消息开始。 Last、LastPerSubject、ByStartSequence 和 ByStartTime 分别从最后一条消息、每个 subject 的最后一条消息、某个序号或某个时间点开始。 该策略只在创建消费者时生效一次；之后，持久化消费者从自己的位置继续。

宏 手写 src/main.rs #[subscriber( JetStreamSubject::new("orders.paid", "ORDERS") .durable("reconciler") .pull_expires(NonZeroDuration::from_secs(nonzero!(1))) )] async fn reconcile(orders: &[Order]) -> HandlerOutcome { let total: u64 = orders.iter().map(|order| order.amount_cents).sum(); tracing::info!(orders = orders.len(), total, "paid orders reconciled"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } src/main.rs struct Reconcile; impl Handle<[Order]> for Reconcile { fn handle( &self, orders: &[Order], _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), Vec<HandlerOutcome>>> { let total: u64 = orders.iter().map(|order| order.amount_cents).sum(); tracing::info!(orders = orders.len(), total, "paid orders reconciled"); ready(Ok(())) } } 接收 &[Order] 的处理器得到一批消息，并为整批只运行一次。 它返回的结果结算这批中的每条消息。

宏 手写 src/main.rs #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App<State = ()> { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("shop", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { b.include(fulfil) .include(show) .include(reconcile.batch(nonzero!(100))) }, ) } src/main.rs fn app() -> impl App<State = ()> { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("shop", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { b.include( subscriber( JetStreamSubject::new("orders.created", "ORDERS").durable("fulfilment"), Fulfil, ) .reply() .build(), ) .include( subscriber( JetStreamSubject::new("orders.*", "ORDERS").deliver_policy(DeliverPolicy::New), Show, ) .build(), ) .include( subscriber( JetStreamSubject::new("orders.paid", "ORDERS") .durable("reconciler") .pull_expires(NonZeroDuration::from_secs(nonzero!(1))), Reconcile, ) .batch(nonzero!(100usize)) .build(), ) }, ) } fn main() -> ExitCode { run_main(app) } 挂载点指定批的大小：batch(100) 在一次拉取中向服务器请求最多一百条消息。 描述符上的 pull_expires 决定一次拉取等待它们多久，这里是一秒，之后交出一个较小的批。 默认值是五秒。 fulfil 的回复通过 Core NATS 发布，这是 Broker 的默认方式。 向流发布则把回复保存到流中。 Core 订阅和 JetStream 订阅共用一个连接，所以一个服务可以自由混用两种模型。 max_ack_pending 限制一个消费者同时持有的未确认投递数；默认值是 1024。 确认与投递保证讲解每次投递如何结算。

本指南为 Core NATS subject 命名，用通配符读取多个 subject，在队列组中让各个副本分担工作，并在并行的工作分区中保持每个键的顺序。 subject 是由点分隔的一串 token，比如 orders.eu.created。 Core NATS 把消息交给此刻 subject 与之匹配的每个订阅，并且什么也不存储。 示例是一个订单服务。 它打包欧洲的订单，为订单开账单，并审计每个地区的每个订单事件。

pack 读取 orders.eu.created。 服务运行多个副本，而每个订单只能打包一次。 宏 手写 src/main.rs #[subscriber(CoreSubject::new("orders.eu.created").queue_group("packers"))] async fn pack(order: &Order) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(order.id, "order packed"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } src/main.rs struct Pack; impl Handle<Order> for Pack { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(order.id, "order packed"); ready(Ok(())) } } CoreSubject 读取一个 subject。 queue_group 把订阅放进 packers 组。 服务器把每条消息交给组内的一个成员，所以每个副本打包一部分订单。 对服务器来说，一个组名就是一个组，即使成员订阅的 subject 不同。 组外的订阅，或者另一个组里的订阅，仍然收到属于自己的一份。

bill 读取同一个 subject，但不加入任何组，所以 pack 收到的每个订单它都会收到。 它最多同时为八个订单开账单，并保持每个客户的顺序。 宏 手写 src/main.rs /// The customer an order belongs to, carried in the partition-key header. #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)] struct CustomerKey { #[serde(rename = "nats-partition-key")] customer: String, } /// The invoice of one order, keyed by the customer like the order it bills. #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, Outgoing)] #[outgoing(name = "invoices.eu", headers = CustomerKey)] struct Invoice { order: u64, amount_cents: u64, } #[derive(OutSlot)] #[publishes(Invoice)] struct Invoices; #[subscriber("orders.eu.created", workers(8, by_key))] async fn bill( order: &Order, Headers(key): Headers<CustomerKey>, Out(invoices): Out<impl Publisher, Invoices>, ) -> HandlerOutcome { let invoice = Invoice { order: order.id, amount_cents: order.amount_cents, }; if invoices .message(&invoice) .with_headers(&key) .publish() .await .is_err() { return HandlerOutcome::retry(); } tracing::info!(order.id, customer = %key.customer, "order billed"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } src/main.rs /// The customer an order belongs to, carried in the partition-key header. #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)] #[schemars(crate = "ruststream::schemars")] struct CustomerKey { #[serde(rename = "nats-partition-key")] customer: String, } /// The invoice of one order, keyed by the customer like the order it bills. #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)] #[schemars(crate = "ruststream::schemars")] struct Invoice { order: u64, amount_cents: u64, } impl OutgoingDestination for Invoice { type Form = FixedName; const DESTINATION: &'static str = "invoices.eu"; } impl MessageHeaders for Invoice { type Contract = WithHeaders<CustomerKey>; } impl MessageInfo for Invoice { const NAME: &'static str = "Invoice"; } struct Invoices; impl OutSlot for Invoices { const NAME: &'static str = "Invoices"; type Destination = Reads; } impl PublishedThrough<Invoices> for Invoice {} struct Bill; impl<Sent> Handle<Message<CustomerKey, Order>, (), Outs<(Sent,)>> for Bill where Sent: OutEntry<Invoices, Wire: Publisher>, { async fn handle( &self, order: &Message<CustomerKey, Order>, outs: &Outs<(Sent,)>, _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> Result<(), HandlerOutcome> { let key = &order.headers; let invoice = Invoice { order: order.body.id, amount_cents: order.body.amount_cents, }; if outs .get(Invoices) .message(&invoice) .with_headers(key) .publish() .await .is_err() { return Err(HandlerOutcome::retry()); } tracing::info!(order.body.id, customer = %key.customer, "order billed"); Ok(()) } } workers(8, by_key) 运行八个工作分区。 键相同的投递在同一个工作分区上依次运行。 在手写形式中，同一设置是 workers_by_key。 NATS 没有原生的键，所以键以 nats-partition-key 消息头（PARTITION_KEY_HEADER）传递，由发送方设置。 CustomerKey 是一个消息头契约，只有一个以该名字命名的字段。 Headers<CustomerKey> 读取投递的键，with_headers(&key) 把它写到账单上。 于是对下一个读者来说，同一客户的账单也保持顺序。 没有该消息头的订单不满足消息头契约，由解码策略结算，默认会丢弃它。 NATS 消息头是文本：名字是不含冒号的可打印 ASCII 字符，值只有一行。 不符合这些要求的消息头会让发布返回错误。
